strings.settings.plugins_hint: Drop a DLL into the plugins folder next to the exe. Each plugin is a card. Search and filter by name, package id, or author.
strings.settings.plugins.settings_off: Enable the plugin to use its settings.
strings.settings.scripting_hint: Python 2 and Python 3 are selected separately. Upcoming Python plugins and the Lua engine will use these paths.

strings.detect.title: Detection
strings.detect.conf.tip.low: Weak or single-indicator match. A lead, not a product identification.
strings.detect.conf.tip.medium: Several independent indicators agree, but the exact product or version is not proven.
strings.detect.conf.tip.high: Strong, distinctive evidence. Still confirm in Hex and Detection details.
strings.detect.conf.tip.exact: Signature evidence is specific enough to name this product with high certainty.
strings.pe.title: Inspector
strings.pe.findings_hint: Evidence-backed interpretation of what this file does and why it matters. Severity is importance; confidence is certainty. This is triage guidance, not a malware verdict.
strings.pe.findings_none: No suspicious structural findings were generated by the enabled analyses.
strings.pe.hex_hint: Click a byte to edit. Drag or Shift+click to select a range. Search AOB (?? wildcards), ASCII, or regex. Unsaved edits are red; saved edits stay blue. Save writes the patched PE.
strings.pe.hex_bad_pat: Invalid AOB. Use hex bytes, 0x, \x, { }, commas; ?? for any byte.

strings.help.fld.file: Full path of the PE currently held in RAM.
strings.help.fld.size: File size in bytes as read from disk.
strings.help.fld.hash: Digest of the original bytes when the file was opened. Hex edits do not refresh hashes until you reopen.
strings.help.fld.imphash: MD5 of the canonical lowercase import list (dll.function), pefile-style. Empty if there are no imports.
strings.help.fld.sha: SHA-256 of the original bytes when the file was opened. Hex edits do not refresh this until you reopen.
strings.help.fld.compiler: Best compiler/toolchain match from the signature library. Expand Detection for evidence and confidence.
strings.help.fld.packer: Best packer match from signatures. Heuristic 'Likely packed' is not a product name. Confirm in Detection.
strings.help.fld.protector: Best protector match from signatures. Generic anti-debug is not treated as a named product.
strings.help.fld.obfuscator: Best .NET obfuscator match. Only runs when a CLR directory is present.
strings.help.fld.arch: COFF Machine: x86, x64, ARM, ... IMAGE_FILE_HEADER.Machine.
strings.help.fld.e_lfanew: IMAGE_DOS_HEADER.e_lfanew: file offset of the PE signature ("PE\0\0") and NT headers. Typical 0x80–0x100.
strings.help.fld.characteristics: IMAGE_FILE_HEADER.Characteristics bitfield (executable, DLL, large address aware, ...).
strings.help.fld.aep: AddressOfEntryPoint: RVA of the first instruction the loader jumps to. Go > Entry point opens Hex there.
strings.help.fld.imagebase: Preferred load address. ASLR may ignore it. PE32 is 32-bit, PE32+ is 64-bit.
strings.help.fld.secalign: Section alignment in memory (usually 0x1000). VirtualAddress values are multiples of this.
strings.help.fld.filealign: Raw section alignment on disk (often 0x200). PointerToRawData is a multiple of this.
strings.help.fld.sizeofimage: Size of the image in memory after sections are mapped. Not the file size.
strings.help.fld.clr: Whether a CLR directory and/or TYPELIB resource is present.
strings.help.fld.overlay: Bytes after the last section raw end. Installer payload, appended data, or leftover signature.
strings.help.fld.secname: 8-byte IMAGE_SECTION_HEADER.Name. Empty or slash names are valid.
strings.help.fld.vaddr: VirtualAddress: RVA where this section is mapped in memory.
strings.help.fld.vsize: Misc.VirtualSize: bytes used in memory. Often larger than SizeOfRawData.
strings.help.fld.rawptr: PointerToRawData: file offset of the section bytes.
strings.help.fld.rawsize: SizeOfRawData: bytes on disk, aligned to FileAlignment.
strings.help.fld.secchars: Section Characteristics: code/data, execute, read, write, discardable.
strings.help.fld.rsrctype: Resource type (RT_ICON, RT_VERSION, RT_MANIFEST, string id, ...).
strings.help.fld.rsrcname: Resource name or numeric id in the directory tree.
strings.help.fld.rsrclang: Language id of this resource leaf.
strings.help.fld.rsrcrva: RVA of the resource data in the mapped image.
strings.help.fld.rsrcoff: File offset of the resource bytes.
strings.help.fld.rsrcsize: Byte length of this resource leaf.
strings.help.fld.dllchars: IMAGE_OPTIONAL_HEADER.DllCharacteristics: NX, ASLR, CFG, high-entropy VA, ...
strings.help.fld.checksum: Optional header CheckSum vs the PE checksum algorithm. Drivers care; user-mode often ignores it.
strings.help.fld.bound: Import descriptor TimeDateStamp is set (bound import).
strings.help.fld.relocs: Base relocation blocks. Page RVA plus type/offset entries.
strings.help.fld.tls: Thread Local Storage directory and callback RVAs (run before entry point).
strings.help.fld.pdb: CodeView RSDS/NB10 PDB path from the debug directory.
strings.pe.rsrc_preview: Select a resource in the list.
strings.pe.analysis_hint: Structures recovered by the Analyze Engine when applicable. Identity detections stay on Detection.
strings.engine.results_hint: Embedded payloads, scripts, metadata tables, and other structures the Analyze Engine recovered automatically. Expand an item to inspect or export it.
strings.engine.results_none: The Analyze Engine did not recover embedded content for this file.
strings.pe.analysis_none: No specialized analysis for this file.
strings.pe.analysis_no_strings: No string constants in this object.
strings.pe.analysis_header_warn: Header magic did not match the expected value. Parsing continued.
strings.pe.analysis_unsupported: Metadata was found, but this version layout is not fully walked.
strings.pe.analysis_partial: Analysis is incomplete because the metadata is truncated or malformed.
strings.pe.analysis_not_source: Recovered bytes are a compiled or encrypted payload, not original source.
strings.pe.analysis_col.name: Name
strings.save.summary_ok: Save completed — patches committed to disk.
strings.save.summary_fail: Save failed — changes remain only in memory.
strings.help.findings: Evidence-backed findings from the Analyze Engine: what was found, why it matters, confidence, and what to inspect next. Severity is importance, not certainty. Click a row for details or jump to Hex when an offset exists. This is triage guidance, not a malware verdict.
strings.find.url.title: URL in strings
strings.find.url.why: Extracted strings contain http(s) or ftp URLs. Often C2, update, or documentation; confirm in Strings.
strings.find.ip.title: IPv4 address in strings
strings.find.ip.why: A dotted IPv4 literal showed up as a whole string. Could be a host, or leftover version-like noise if it looks too small.
strings.find.email.title: Email-like string
strings.find.email.why: A compact token with @ and a domain dot. Contact, license, or exfil destination.
strings.find.unc.title: UNC path in strings
strings.find.unc.why: \\server\share style path. Lateral copy or config drop.
strings.find.onion.title: Onion address in strings
strings.find.onion.why: .onion host in strings. Typical of Tor C2; rare in clean software.
strings.find.runkey.title: Autorun / IFEO string
strings.find.runkey.why: Run key, UserInit, or Image File Execution Options text. Persistence candidate.
strings.find.lolbin.title: LOLBin / interpreter string
strings.find.lolbin.why: powershell, cmd, wscript, mshta, rundll32, schtasks, certutil, or similar. Living-off-the-land execution.
strings.find.inject.title: Process injection APIs
strings.find.inject.why: Imports include classic remote-alloc / write / remote-thread or section-map helpers.
strings.find.netapi.title: Network / download APIs
strings.find.netapi.why: WinINet, WinHTTP, URLDownload, or BSD sockets in the IAT. Reach-out capability.
strings.find.spawn.title: Process spawn APIs
strings.find.spawn.why: CreateProcess / ShellExecute / WinExec imported. Child process launch.
strings.find.crypto.title: Crypto APIs
strings.find.crypto.why: CryptoAPI or BCrypt encrypt/decrypt in the IAT. Packing, licensing, or payload decode.
strings.find.antidebug.title: Anti-debug APIs
strings.find.antidebug.why: IsDebuggerPresent or related imports. Common in protectors and malware; also in some games.
strings.find.mutex.title: Mutex APIs
strings.find.mutex.why: CreateMutex / OpenMutex. Single-instance lock or infection marker.
strings.find.regwrite.title: Registry write APIs
strings.find.regwrite.why: RegSetValue / RegCreateKey in the IAT. Config or persistence.
strings.find.packer.title: Named packer / wrapper
strings.find.packer.why: Signature engine identified a packer or script wrapper. See Detection for evidence.
strings.find.compiler.title: Non-MSVC compiler identity
strings.find.compiler.why: Compiler/toolchain match other than generic MSVC. See Detection.
strings.find.dos.title: Unusual DOS stub size
strings.find.dos.why: e_lfanew is larger than a typical DOS stub. Extra data or a patched stub before PE.
strings.find.nosec.title: No sections
strings.find.nosec.why: NumberOfSections is 0. Broken or hand-crafted image.
strings.find.ts.title: Suspicious timestamp
strings.find.ts.why: COFF TimeDateStamp is 0 or 0xFFFFFFFF. Often stripped or backdated.
strings.find.nx.title: NX / DEP not requested
strings.find.nx.why: NX_COMPAT is clear. The image does not ask the loader for DEP.
strings.find.aslr.title: ASLR not requested
strings.find.aslr.why: DYNAMIC_BASE is clear. Preferred ImageBase is more likely to stick.
strings.find.cksum.title: Checksum mismatch
strings.find.cksum.why: Optional header CheckSum is set but does not match the computed value. Patch, copy, or unsigned edit.
strings.find.wx.title: Writable + executable section
strings.find.wx.why: A section is both writable and executable. Common in packers and self-modifying stubs.
strings.find.vsize.title: Section virtual end past SizeOfImage
strings.find.vsize.why: VirtualAddress + VirtualSize exceeds SizeOfImage. Loader vs parser mismatch risk.
strings.find.overlay.title: Overlay present
strings.find.overlay.why: Bytes exist after the last section raw end. Installer payload, appended archive, or compiled script blob.
strings.find.epout.title: Entry point outside sections
strings.find.epout.why: AddressOfEntryPoint does not land in a section. Packed, damaged, or header-executed.
strings.find.epsec.title: Entry in packer section
strings.find.epsec.why: Entry point section name matches a known packer stub (UPX, Themida, ASPack).
strings.find.noimp.title: No imports (EXE)
strings.find.noimp.why: This EXE has an empty import table. Typical of packers that rebuild the IAT at runtime.
strings.find.tls.title: TLS callbacks
strings.find.tls.why: TLS directory lists callbacks. They run before the entry point; packers and anti-debug use this.
strings.find.pdb.title: PDB path present
strings.find.pdb.why: Debug directory carries a PDB path. Build machine / project leak.
strings.find.entropy.title: High entropy range
strings.find.entropy.why: A mapped range is near-random (>= 7.0). Packed, encrypted, or compressed payload.
strings.find.align.title: Zero alignment
strings.find.align.why: SectionAlignment or FileAlignment is 0. Not a well-formed PE.
strings.finding.summary.title: Analysis Summary
strings.finding.summary.packed: This executable shows signs of packing or protection.
strings.finding.summary.indicators: This file has structural indicators worth reviewing.
strings.finding.summary.none: No major suspicious structural indicators were found by the enabled analyses.
strings.finding.summary.disclaimer: This does not guarantee the file is safe. Static analysis can miss runtime behavior.
strings.finding.detail.title: What we found
strings.finding.detail.pick: Select a finding to read the full explanation.
strings.finding.section.rwx.title: Part of this program can change itself and run code
strings.finding.section.rwx.explain: One section is marked as both writable and executable.
strings.finding.section.rwx.matter: Normal program code usually does not need permission to rewrite itself. Packers, protectors, and some malicious software use this layout.
strings.finding.section.rwx.next: Inspect the section in Hex and review Packing / Protection detections.
strings.finding.overlay.title: Extra data exists after the normal executable ends
strings.finding.overlay.explain: This file contains bytes appended after the last PE section.
strings.finding.overlay.matter: Installers, packers, and some malware store additional payloads or configuration in this area.
strings.finding.overlay.next: Inspect the extra data in Hex or open the Overlay view.
strings.finding.overlay.tech: Technical: PE overlay bytes after the mapped image.
strings.finding.entropy.title: A section looks compressed or encrypted
strings.finding.entropy.explain: Part of this file looks unusually random.
strings.finding.entropy.matter: Normal program code usually contains recognizable patterns. High randomness often appears when data is compressed, encrypted, or packed.
strings.finding.entropy.next: Inspect the section in Hex and review packer/protector detections.
strings.finding.entropy.tech: Technical: Shannon entropy near 8.0 in a mapped range.
strings.finding.tls.title: Code may run before the normal starting point
strings.finding.tls.matter: TLS callbacks execute before the program's main entry point. Protectors and malware sometimes use them to hide initialization or anti-analysis code.
strings.finding.tls.next: Open the TLS view and inspect callback targets in Hex.
strings.finding.tls.tech: Technical: Thread Local Storage callback RVAs are present.
strings.finding.import.inject.title: This program imports process-modification APIs
strings.finding.import.inject.explain: The import table includes functions commonly used to allocate memory in another process and modify it.
strings.finding.import.inject.matter: This does not prove malicious behavior, but the combination is worth investigating.
strings.finding.import.inject.next: Review the Imports list and related strings.
strings.finding.import.inject.tech: Technical: remote allocation / write / thread or section-map imports.
strings.finding.import.network.title: This program imports network or download APIs
strings.finding.import.network.explain: The import table includes functions used to connect, send, or download data.
strings.finding.import.network.matter: Legitimate updaters use these too, but they are common in droppers and downloaders.
strings.finding.import.network.next: Review Strings and Imports for URLs or hosts.
strings.finding.import.network.tech: Technical: WinINet, WinHTTP, URLDownload, or socket imports.
strings.finding.import.none.title: This executable imports almost nothing
strings.finding.import.none.explain: The import table is empty or nearly empty.
strings.finding.import.none.matter: Packers often hide imports until runtime. Some tiny or hand-built programs also do this.
strings.finding.import.none.next: Review entry point bytes, entropy, and packer detections.
strings.finding.import.none.tech: Technical: empty Import Directory on an EXE.
strings.finding.embedded.title: Embedded content was recovered
strings.finding.embedded.explain: The Analyze Engine extracted one or more embedded structures from this file.
strings.finding.embedded.matter: The file may contain scripts, bytecode, archives, or other payloads not visible in the main PE layout alone.
strings.finding.embedded.next: Open Extracted Content and inspect the recovered items.
strings.finding.corr.packed.title: Several signs suggest this executable may be packed
strings.finding.corr.packed.explain: Multiple independent indicators point toward packing or protection.
strings.finding.corr.packed.matter: This is a heuristic conclusion, not a product identification. Confirm in Detection and Hex.
strings.finding.corr.packed.next: Inspect high-entropy sections, imports, and Detection evidence.
strings.finding.corr.packed.tech: Technical: correlated entropy, import, and layout indicators.
strings.finding.detect.packer.title: A packer or wrapper was detected
strings.finding.detect.packer.explain: Signature evidence matched a known packer or script wrapper.
strings.finding.detect.packer.matter: The file may contain compressed or transformed code that is unpacked at runtime.
strings.finding.detect.packer.next: Open Detection for evidence and inspect the entry section in Hex.
strings.finding.detect.protector.title: A protector was detected
strings.finding.detect.protector.explain: Signature evidence matched a known code protector.
strings.finding.detect.protector.matter: Protected binaries often hide code, resist debugging, or decrypt at runtime.
strings.finding.detect.protector.next: Review Detection evidence and the entry section layout.
strings.finding.detect.compiler.title: An unusual compiler or toolchain was detected
strings.finding.detect.compiler.explain: Signature evidence matched a non-default compiler or toolchain.
strings.finding.detect.compiler.matter: This helps explain how the binary was built and which analysis paths may apply.
strings.finding.entry.sec.title: The program starts inside an unusual section
strings.finding.entry.sec.explain: The entry point is not in a typical code section name.
strings.finding.entry.sec.matter: Packers and protectors often move startup code into a custom section.
strings.finding.entry.sec.next: Open the entry point in Hex and review section entropy.
strings.finding.string.url.title: A web address appears in readable strings
strings.finding.string.url.explain: The file contains http, https, or ftp URLs in extracted strings.
strings.finding.string.url.matter: URLs can point to updates, documentation, command-and-control, or download locations.
strings.finding.string.url.next: Open Strings and inspect the surrounding context.
strings.finding.string.ip.title: An IP address appears in readable strings
strings.finding.string.ip.explain: A dotted IPv4 address was found as a standalone string.
strings.finding.string.ip.matter: It may be a host, configuration value, or leftover noise.
strings.finding.string.ip.next: Open Strings and verify the surrounding context.
strings.finding.string.ip.tech: Technical: IPv4 literal in extracted strings.
strings.finding.string.email.title: An email-like string was found
strings.finding.string.email.explain: A token resembling an email address appears in strings.
strings.finding.string.email.matter: It may be contact information, licensing data, or an exfil destination.
strings.finding.string.email.next: Inspect the string in context on the Strings page.
strings.finding.string.unc.title: A network share path appears in strings
strings.finding.string.unc.matter: This can indicate lateral copy, staging, or configuration paths.
strings.finding.string.unc.next: Inspect the string on the Strings page.
strings.finding.string.onion.title: A Tor onion address appears in strings
strings.finding.string.onion.matter: Onion addresses are uncommon in typical commercial software and often relate to hidden services.
strings.finding.string.onion.next: Inspect the string and surrounding context.
strings.finding.string.runkey.title: Autostart-related registry text was found
strings.finding.string.runkey.explain: Strings mention Run keys, UserInit, or Image File Execution Options.
strings.finding.string.runkey.matter: These locations are commonly used for persistence.
strings.finding.string.runkey.next: Inspect the matching strings and imports.
strings.finding.string.lolbin.title: Living-off-the-land tool names appear in strings
strings.finding.string.lolbin.explain: Strings mention powershell, cmd, wscript, mshta, rundll32, or similar tools.
strings.finding.string.lolbin.matter: These names often appear when a program launches other system tools.
strings.finding.string.lolbin.next: Inspect the strings and process-spawn imports.
strings.finding.import.spawn.title: This program can launch other processes
strings.finding.import.spawn.explain: The import table includes CreateProcess or ShellExecute family APIs.
strings.finding.import.spawn.matter: Many legitimate programs spawn helpers, but this is also common in droppers.
strings.finding.import.crypto.title: This program imports encryption APIs
strings.finding.import.crypto.explain: CryptoAPI or BCrypt encrypt/decrypt functions are imported.
strings.finding.import.crypto.matter: Encryption may protect data, licensing, or packed payloads.
strings.finding.import.crypto.next: Review high-entropy regions and embedded content.
strings.finding.import.antidebug.title: This program imports anti-debug APIs
strings.finding.import.antidebug.explain: Debugger detection functions are present in the import table.
strings.finding.import.antidebug.matter: Protectors, games, and malware use these to detect analysis environments.
strings.finding.import.antidebug.next: Review execution-related findings and entry behavior.
strings.finding.import.mutex.title: This program imports mutex APIs
strings.finding.import.mutex.explain: CreateMutex or OpenMutex functions are imported.
strings.finding.import.mutex.matter: Programs use mutexes for single-instance locking or infection markers.
strings.finding.import.regwrite.title: This program can write to the registry
strings.finding.import.regwrite.matter: Registry writes may configure the program or establish persistence.
strings.finding.header.dos.title: The DOS header area is unusually large
strings.finding.header.dos.explain: The PE header starts farther into the file than usual.
strings.finding.header.dos.matter: Extra space before the PE header can hide data or indicate a modified stub.
strings.finding.header.dos.next: Inspect the start of the file in Hex.
strings.finding.header.nosec.title: This PE reports zero sections
strings.finding.header.nosec.matter: A valid PE normally has at least one section. This may be malformed or intentionally unusual.
strings.finding.header.ts.title: The build timestamp looks suspicious
strings.finding.header.ts.explain: The COFF timestamp is zero or all bits set.
strings.finding.header.ts.matter: Authors sometimes strip or fake timestamps during repacking or rebuilding.
strings.finding.header.ts.next: Compare with Detection and version resources.
strings.finding.hardening.nx.title: DEP was not requested for this image
strings.finding.hardening.nx.explain: The PE header does not ask the loader to enable Data Execution Prevention.
strings.finding.hardening.nx.matter: Modern Windows software usually opts into DEP.
strings.finding.hardening.nx.next: Review other hardening flags in Headers.
strings.finding.hardening.aslr.title: ASLR was not requested for this image
strings.finding.hardening.aslr.explain: The PE header does not ask for address-space randomization.
strings.finding.hardening.aslr.matter: Without ASLR, the program is more likely to load at a predictable address.
strings.finding.integrity.cksum.title: The PE checksum does not match
strings.finding.integrity.cksum.explain: The stored checksum differs from the computed value.
strings.finding.integrity.cksum.matter: This often happens after patching, copying, or rebuilding the file.
strings.finding.integrity.cksum.next: Review recent edits in Changes and Hex.
strings.finding.section.vsize.title: A section extends past the image size
strings.finding.section.vsize.explain: A section's virtual end exceeds SizeOfImage.
strings.finding.section.vsize.matter: This can indicate a malformed header or deliberate layout manipulation.
strings.finding.section.vsize.next: Inspect the section table and Hex layout.
strings.finding.entry.out.title: The entry point is outside all sections
strings.finding.entry.out.explain: AddressOfEntryPoint does not map to a section.
strings.finding.entry.out.matter: This can happen with packing, damage, or header-executed stubs.
strings.finding.entry.out.next: Open the entry point in Hex.
strings.finding.entry.out.tech: Technical: entry RVA not contained in any section.
strings.finding.pdb.title: A debug symbol path is present
strings.finding.pdb.explain: The debug directory contains a PDB path.
strings.finding.pdb.matter: This can reveal build machine paths or internal project names.
strings.finding.pdb.next: Inspect the Debug view and path string.
strings.finding.header.align.title: Section or file alignment is zero
strings.finding.header.align.matter: Well-formed PE files use non-zero alignment values.
strings.finding.header.align.next: Inspect the optional header in Hex.
strings.help.overview: File identity: path, size, hashes, signature-based compiler/packer/protector summary, machine, subsystem, entry, image base. .NET obfuscator only appears for CLR images. Detection pane has evidence. Nothing here writes the file until you Save from File.
strings.help.headers: DOS stub + COFF/optional header fields (e_lfanew, characteristics, alignments, SizeOfImage, Rich if present). These are parsed facts. Editing them is not in this pane; use Hex if you must poke the header bytes, then Save.
strings.help.sections: IMAGE_SECTION_HEADER table. This page lists every section (.text, .rdata, .rsrc, ...); select a row for VirtualAddress / PointerToRawData. Expand is not in the tree — the list lives here.
strings.help.section: One PE section. VirtualSize vs SizeOfRawData often differ (virtual is in memory, raw is on disk). Characteristics bits say execute/read/write. Jump to PointerToRawData in Hex to see the bytes.
strings.help.imports: Import Directory: DLLs this image binds at load. The tree node opens this page; the list is DLLs, functions are names or ordinals. Unpacking/malware often hide or smash this table. Read-only here.
strings.help.import: Imported DLL and its IAT names. These strings live in the file; changing them in Hex can break the loader. No in-place import editor yet.
strings.help.exports: Export Directory: names/ordinals this DLL (or exe) exposes. Read-only list of AddressOfFunctions / names.
strings.help.hex: Byte editor over the whole file image held in RAM. Drag to select a range. Search AOB with ?? wildcards, ASCII, or regex (Ctrl+F). Unsaved bytes are red; after Save they stay blue for this session. Edits do not hit disk until File > Save.
strings.help.hex_search: AOB: 48 8B ?? 90, 488B??90, 0x48 0x8B, \x48\x8B, {0x48,??}. ASCII/SOB is a literal byte string. Regex is ECMAScript over the 8-bit image.
strings.help.resources: PE resource directory (.rsrc): icons, version, dialogs, manifests, typelibs, and the rest. Tree node is a leaf. This page is list+preview; All / Version / Icons / COM filter the list. Specialized payloads also appear under Specialized Analysis. Orange ! means a resource patch is still only in RAM.
strings.help.version: RT_VERSION / VS_VERSIONINFO. FileVersion and ProductVersion plus the string table (FileDescription, ProductName, ...). Edits patch the existing resource slot in RAM. A longer string only fits if the original node has slack. Save writes the PE.
strings.help.icons: RT_GROUP_ICON + RT_ICON. List on the left, preview/export/replace on the right. Replace requires the new image to be the same byte size as the original RT_ICON (in-place, not a resource rebuild). Unsaved replace shows ! until Save.
strings.help.com: CLR (IMAGE_COR20_HEADER) and TYPELIB blobs. .NET runtime version/flags and MSFT typelib version dword. Not a full COM type library editor. Patches stay in RAM until Save.
strings.help.overlay: Bytes after the last section's raw end. Often installer payload, signature leftovers, or appended data. Size/offset only; open Hex at that offset to inspect.
strings.help.detection: Signature matches for packers, protectors, compilers/toolchains, and .NET obfuscators. Each row has a product, confidence, source (built-in / pack / user), and evidence. Expand for signature IDs. Heuristics are labelled and are not product identifications.
strings.help.analysis: Generic view of structures extracted by specialized analyzers. Identity detections stay on Detection. Providers register by capability (resource type, product_key), not by product name in the UI.
strings.help.patch: Patch journal of in-memory edits. Unsaved bytes are red; saved patches stay blue until you undo them. Undo after Save is an unsaved difference vs the last written file. Ctrl+Z in Hex or Changes reverts the last patch; text fields keep their own undo.
strings.patch.title: Changes
strings.patch.hint: Byte patches against the loaded image. Save writes the working buffer and keeps this history. Undo after Save marks bytes unsaved even if they match the original disk bytes.
strings.tool.missing: DecompSnake is not available. Build decompsnake.dll and place it beside the exe.
strings.tool.bad_input: This artifact has no usable Python bytecode.
strings.tool.unsupported_bytecode: This Python bytecode version is not supported.
